turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm trying to cut our grocery bill and I can't decide where to do the weekly shop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me finish describing every option before you respond.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our usual big supermarket has everything in one place and good loyalty points, but I always overspend there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The discount shop across town is way cheaper, though the range is small and it's a twenty minute drive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We could do online delivery, no impulse buys, but there's a fee and sometimes they swap things.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or the Saturday market for veg and the corner shop for the rest, which is fun but takes ages.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's all of them. What do you think?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If overspending is the problem, online delivery might actually save you money even with the fee, because you only buy what's on the list. The discount shop is cheapest per item, but the drive eats into it. The market is lovely, just not when you're short on time.
